title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure rather than a model error. A person's face is placed onto pornographic footage and the result is published as if it depicted her, so the false claim is carried by the image itself and needs no text to be believed. The people affected are named public figures, including entertainers, presenters, athletes, ministers, mayors and members of the Royal Family, and the reporting describes them discovering the material rather than consenting to it.

The failure sits in a user-upload platform, not in a single model. That platform reportedly tells uploaders to stay anonymous and pays them more when videos are watched often, which means the incentive to post and the incentive to hide point the same way. Catching this at the point of upload would have required the platform to check what was being posted and to know who was posting it, and neither check is described in the reporting. What followed was complaints to authorities, a parliamentary motion to designate a body able to take such images offline, and, as reported, parliamentarians hearing nothing for months after the initial attention.

What is not established is who made the videos, whether the platform bears legal responsibility, and whether any of the complaints will result in charges. A filed report is not a finding, and the earlier case described in the reporting is a separate matter.

summary:
Several Dutch female celebrities are considering legal action after discovering themselves in fabricated pornographic videos posted on an online platform with 13 million monthly visitors. The videos feature manipulated content involving Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government ministers, mayors, and members of the Royal Family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and encouraged victims to file complaints. Managers and representatives of various victims confirmed to news outlets that they have filed reports or are pursuing legal action.

These deepfake videos work by placing a celebrity's face onto pornographic footage. The platform reportedly advises users who upload such material to remain anonymous, likely to avoid prosecution, and pays them more money if videos receive many views. Legal experts warn that without government intervention, more fake pornographic videos featuring celebrities will appear. Deepfakes fall under revenge pornography laws and are prosecutable. Victims can file complaints with authorities who may shut down the website, start group lawsuits, file complaints with data protection agencies, or contact hosting companies. One previous case resulted in a 39-year-old man receiving a conditional 180-hour task sentence.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
